V2-Q0712.clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: The nurse is selecting a needle for an injectable vaccine. Which set of factors should guide the selection?

options.A: Route of administration, patient age, sex and weight for adults aged 19 years and older, injection site, and injection technique.
options.B: Vaccine brand, vial presentation, expiration date, the client’s dominant arm, prior injection-site soreness, and dose number in the series.
options.C: Patient age, preferred arm, vaccine manufacturer, vial size, history of post-vaccination fever, and number of vaccines due at the visit.
options.D: Route of administration, injection site, dose schedule, storage temperature, lot number, and whether the vaccine is supplied in a vial or syringe.

semantic_correction.rationale: CDC vaccine-administration guidance lists route of administration, patient age, sex and weight for adults aged 19 years and older, injection site, and injection technique as the factors on which needle selection should be based; it also directs clinicians to use clinical judgment. Option A contains that set. Options B, C, and D mix some vaccine-administration details with factors that are not part of CDC’s listed needle-selection set, so they do not provide the complete guidance for needle selection.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Select a vaccine-administration needle using the CDC factors of route, patient age, adult sex and weight, injection site, and injection technique.
semantic_correction.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: Needle selection for injectable vaccines should be based on route of administration, patient age, sex and weight for adults aged 19 years and older, injection site, and injection technique, with clinical judgment used in selection.

audit_findings_append.finding: Original correct answer was source-supported, but the original distractors used obvious absolute/cueing language (every/regardless/only/default) and were not acceptable for final bank quality. Distractors were rebuilt with clinically adjacent vaccine-administration details while retaining one uniquely best answer.

option_audit.A: Correct. Matches the CDC Needle Selection factor set.
option_audit.B: Plausible vaccine-administration context, but does not match the CDC needle-selection factor set.
option_audit.C: Contains patient age but substitutes other vaccine-care details for the required CDC factors; not a complete needle-selection set.
option_audit.D: Contains route and injection site but substitutes schedule/storage/lot/presentation details and omits required patient and technique factors; not the best answer.
